20. Primarily known as common pantry pests that feed on dried meats and cheeses, these beetles can occasionally find a niche on the human body. They are scavengers rather than true parasites, feeding on dead skin, shed hair, and other organic debris, particularly in individuals with limited mobility. Their larvae are covered in tiny, irritating hairs that can cause a specific type of dermatitis. Name the beetle.

21. This nocturnal insect is the subject of a famous but largely exaggerated myth regarding its tendency to enter the ear canal. While the stories of them burrowing into the brain are false, they do seek out tight, dark, and moist spaces for shelter. For those sleeping outdoors or camping, this insect may occasionally wander into an ear simply because it provides a convenient hiding spot. Identify it.
